# Slice 1, worked by seen-implementer on sonnet, and one thing to carry forward

Slice 1 was delegated, as its route record said: `seen-implementer` on sonnet at high effort wrote
the RED at record 9, the code, and the GREEN at record 11. Record 10 is a GREEN it superseded with a
wording fix to the refusal message and re-ran, which is why two greens sit beside one red.

Two things the next session needs and cannot infer.

**The checks of slice 1 declare no agent.** The spawn instruction this session wrote gave the check
command without `--agent`, because `--agent` is the flag slice 1 adds and did not exist when the
instruction was written. Nothing refuses on it: `[routing] shadow` is true, so
`_require_a_context_of_its_own` returns before it reads anything. It is recorded here rather than
corrected, because correcting it would mean this session re-running a check a subagent ran and
declaring an agent it was not: the flag is a disclosure, and a disclosure typed by the wrong party is
the one thing it must never be. Slices 2 and 3 pass `--agent seen-implementer`, which is honest
because their implementer runs them.

**The session that planned this ticket was over budget before a line was written.** 61,432 output
tokens against 60,000 at the moment slice 1 was handed over, all of it clarify and solution. That is
the ticket's own thesis measured on the ticket itself, and it is the figure slice 2's forecast should
be read against: a plan whose planning alone exceeds the budget is not a plan a per-slice prediction
can rescue. Worth a line in the Outcome.
